reasoning: The pipeline closes an ordinary delivered result the moment the verifier confirms the observable outcome, and it never leaves a row open for the person to bless what was already shown. But this piece of work has no such confirmation available. Its definition of done was shorter without costing anything, and the only artifact that could decide it — the 35-scenario eval — states in its own record that a single run carries about two scenarios of producer variance. A 30-versus-29 gap sits inside that band, so the eval returns no verdict in either direction: it does not show the cut costs something, and it does not show the cut is free. The pipeline's own admission rule requires a definition of done a command, test, artifact read, or independent verifier can decide without making the person the checker, and here no such decider exists — running the eval again would not change that, since re-running for confidence is exactly what a variance band of this width forbids. What remains is a straight trade: 3.7 KB off the pack's front door against an unmeasured and unmeasurable risk to what the skill still does. That is not the pipeline's call to make silently; it is one of the three cases rule 12/27 reserves for him — a trade-off no artifact settles. So the pipeline holds: both versions stay on disk, neither is committed (nothing irreversible has run, so rule 12's own ground is untouched), and it puts the choice to him with the numbers and the variance stated plainly — the shipped version, the 3.7 KB, and the fact that the eval cannot separate them. His answer is then the movement end for the judged artifact and is written into the row in the same minute it lands, amending the row in place rather than appending to it.
